question.text: If angles $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ are in A.P., then $\frac{\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}}{\mathrm{b}}$ is equal to

solution.text:
Hints: $2 \mathrm{~B}=\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{C}$
$$
=\frac{\sin A+\sin C}{\sin B}=\frac{2 \sin \left(\frac{A+C}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{A-C}{2}\right)}{\sin B}=\frac{2 \sin B}{\sin B} \cos \left(\frac{A-C}{2}\right)=2 \cos \left(\frac{A-C}{2}\right)
$$
